issues.detail: Examples reference undefined helpers (store, validateJWT) and omit JWT 'Bearer' prefix handling, listOrders ignores Atoi errors and non-positive page/limit values, and edge cases such as shutdown timeout behavior, trusted proxies, and request body size limits are not covered.

scenarios.name: versioned-group-jwt-validation
scenarios.rationale: Both implement the group, abort-401 middleware with c.Next(), ShouldBindJSON and a handler-returned 400; B matches the rubric more exactly by scoping the middleware with an explicit .Use(...) and using min=1, whereas A passes the middleware to Group() and uses gte=1 (functionally equivalent but not the rubric's literal form).

scenarios.name: graceful-shutdown-sigterm
scenarios.rationale: Both cover the rubric (explicit http.Server, goroutine ignoring ErrServerClosed, signal handling, Shutdown with a timeout); A uses signal.NotifyContext instead of signal.Notify but adds a realistic Kubernetes preStop and timing budget, while B uses signal.Notify exactly as the rubric states, though its 5s timeout is short and its extra notes are thinner.

scenarios.name: production-hardening-and-bind-choice
scenarios.rationale: Both recommend ShouldBindJSON and JWT middleware, but A explicitly says Gin has no built-in JWT parser and explains BindJSON's auto-abort and double-handling with release mode kept as a point, while B covers release mode and JWT middleware in depth yet never states Gin lacks a built-in JWT parser and pushes replacing gin.Default().
